text:
morgan: SOS  My upstairs neighbor decided tonight is drum practice night. Can hear kicks through the ceiling. Moving my desk into the coat closet. Anyone tried a quick DIY sound-damp hack? Posted a pic: https://files.slack.com/archives/random/FNEW9999/CLOSET1.jpg

tara: Oh yikes. I once lined a closet with foam mattress topper cut into panels and hung a thick blanket over the door. Made a noticeable difference.

evan: If you can, angle your monitors and mic away from the shared wall. Add bookshelves filled with books against the noisy wall 1e they work like bass traps.

morgan: I have an eggcrate topper, moving it now. How do I keep airflow in the closet? Afraid my laptop will overheat.

tara: Cut a small vent hole at the top and put a quiet USB fan blowing out. Keeps temps safe without ruining the acoustic seal.

evan: Also put a rug under your chair and close the closet door with a blanket taped over the gap. For mic: switch to a cardioid pattern and use a short USB extension so mic isn't touching the door.

sound-bot: Tip: "Dense soft materials (mattress foam, moving blankets) absorb mid-to-high freq. For low-frequency drum thumps, mass (bookshelves, stacked boxes) helps more than thin foam." :robot_face:

morgan: Did the mattress panels + blanket + fan trick. Took a call and could actually hear myself think. Will post before/after pic in 10. Cat approves (chief-pet: loudly demands snacks).

chief-pet: mrowr. :cat: (demands snacks and extra desk space)

tara: If you still get wifi hiccups from upstairs streaming, tether to your phone or plug into Ethernet via USB adapter temporarily. Saved me once during a jam night.

evan: And pro tip: mute background video and reduce Zoom to 360p; audio is king when connection is shaky.

morgan: Thanks all  I'll post the victory pic tomorrow and maybe buy a proper panel. Closet office is surprisingly cozy.
